title: Bug: on-deck tasks not auto-promoting to in-progress when agent capacity opens
description:
## Bug
When an agent finishes a build, on-deck tasks assigned to that agent do not auto-promote to in-progress. The reconciler runs every 15s but fails to detect open capacity and promote the next task. Tim and Henry have been manually promoting tasks all night.

## Expected Behavior
1. Agent finishes build → slot opens
2. Reconciler detects agent has no active build
3. Top on-deck task for that agent auto-promotes to in-progress
4. Build auto-spawns
5. Zero human intervention

## Current Behavior
Tasks sit in on-deck indefinitely. Manual PATCH required to move them. The advanceTasks() function in build-queue.ts exists but is not triggering reliably.

## Root Cause Investigation
- Check advanceTasks() in reconcileBuildQueue — is it being called?
- Check findActiveBuildForAgent — is it returning stale entries that block promotion?
- Check if build-log.json has orphaned running entries that make the pipeline think agents are busy
- The reconciler may not be matching agent IDs correctly (Forge vs backend vs forge)

## Fix
Make auto-promote reliable. When an agent has zero active builds and there are on-deck tasks assigned to them, promote immediately. No human in the loop.

## This is the #1 autonomy blocker after Gater auto-spawn.

## Summary

**Root cause:** Two bugs in `advanceTasks()` (`build-queue.ts:1237-1254`):

1. **Per-project blocking instead of per-agent** — `hasInProgressBuild` checked if ANY in-progress task in the same project had a pending build entry. If agent A was building task X, agent B's on-deck task Y would never promote, even though B was idle.

2. **Single-candidate bottleneck** — only `onDeck[0]` was evaluated per cycle. Even with multiple idle agents, only one task per project could promote per reconciler run.

**Fix:** Replaced the per-project `hasInProgressBuild` check with per-agent capacity checks using the existing `findActiveBuildForAgent()`. Now iterates all on-deck candidates, promoting each one whose assigned agent is idle and whose execution key hasn't hit the concurrency cap.

- Tasks without a pre-assigned agent will have `resolveAgentForTask()` called during promotion to determine the agent — this is the same function `autoAssignBuilder` uses, so it's consistent.

title: Live build activity stream on task cards — show what the agent is doing in real-time
description:
## Inspiration
Paperclip shows live agent activity directly on the task: READ COMPLETED, WRITE COMPLETED, agent reasoning text, file paths being modified. You can watch the agent work in real-time. Our task cards are completely blind — you see a glow and nothing else until it is done.

## What To Build
1. When an agent is actively building a task, stream their tool calls and reasoning to the task card
2. Show each action as a line item: READ file.ts COMPLETED, WRITE component.tsx COMPLETED, RUN npm build COMPLETED
3. The task card expands vertically to show this activity feed while the agent is working
4. When the build completes, the activity log becomes the build history stored in comments
5. Real-time updates via WebSocket or SSE — no polling

## UX
- Collapsed by default on non-active tasks
- Auto-expanded when buildState=running with live streaming activity
- Each line: checkmark + action type (READ/WRITE/RUN/THINK) + description + COMPLETED/RUNNING status
- Scrolls to latest action automatically
- When build finishes, collapses back to summary

## This is the difference between watching a dashboard and watching a team work. Tim should be able to see exactly what Forge or Pixel is doing at any moment without opening a separate tool.

title: Auto-spawn Gater when task hits review — real agent, not just a label
description:
## Bug
autoAssignGater() in build-queue.ts only puts Gaters name on the task. It does NOT spawn her as a Claude process to actually do the QA. Henry has been manually spawning Gater every time, which defeats the purpose of autonomy.

## Fix
Create spawnGaterQAProcess() that:
1. Fires when ANY task moves to review status
2. Spawns Claude with Gater identity, Playwright instructions, the task context
3. Gater runs build verification, dual-browser screenshots, code review
4. Gater approves (moves to done) or rejects (moves back to in-progress with notes)
5. No human in the loop. Henry does not need to trigger this.

Model it after spawnVigilQAProcess() which already exists for automated QA.

This is the #1 autonomy blocker. Without this, every review requires Henry to manually wake Gater, which means reviews sit until Henrys next heartbeat.

## Key Files
- src/lib/build-queue.ts — autoAssignGater, spawnVigilQAProcess (reference)
- The Gater prompt should include: run npm build, Playwright Chromium+WebKit screenshots, code diff review, approve/reject with structured comments

## Bug
The factory spawns multiple concurrent builds for the same agent. If Forge has 3 tasks in-progress, all 3 get a Claude process and all 3 glow. This is wrong — a real engineer works one task at a time.

## What It Does
1. When a build completes on any UI task (tags: ui, frontend, component, page), auto-capture a screenshot of the affected page(s)
2. Store before/after screenshots in the task's attachments

- No human QA needed for routine UI tasks

title: Design Spec: Weather Trading Tournament Architecture
description:
Design the full tournament architecture for competitive weather trading across multiple teams. This is a DESIGN SPEC — not a build task. Must be reviewed by Tim before any code is written.

## Context
We have multiple teams producing weather trading signals:
1. **Internal team** (Nimbus/Quant) — our model watcher + scanner pipeline
2. **Weather Edge** (Paperclip company) — Ridge's team with their own scanner
3. **Cliff's team** — independent setup on his own OpenClaw instance
4. **Martin's team** — benchmarking only, not rotated into live trading

All teams compete. Best performer gets live Kalshi capital each week. Others paper trade. Martin's team participates in the leaderboard but doesn't get live capital rotation.

## Design Requirements

### 1. Standardized Signal Format
- Universal schema all teams must output
- Fields: city, contract_type, direction, confidence, recommended_size, model_sources, timestamp, team_id
- Must be simple enough for Cliff and Martin to adopt on their setups
- JSON or simple API endpoint

### 2. Single Source of Truth — Performance Database
- Centralized performance tracking (Supabase? SQLite?)
- Every signal from every team logged with outcome
- Reconciled against actual Kalshi market settlements
- Clean separation: paper signals vs live executions
- P&L, win rate, Sharpe ratio, calibration score per team per period

### 3. Tournament Evaluator
- Weekly evaluation cycle (Sunday night?)
- Scoring criteria: Sharpe ratio (primary), win rate, total P&L, calibration accuracy, max drawdown
- Winner gets live executor for the following week
- Ties broken by calibration accuracy (our real edge)
- Minimum sample size: team must have produced 10+ signals to qualify

### 4. Live Executor Switcher
- Config flag: active_strategy = "internal" | "weather_edge" | "cliff"
- Model watcher reads signals from winning team's output
- Clean handoff — no position conflicts, no overlapping bets
- Kill switch still works regardless of active team

### 5. Leaderboard Dashboard (Mission Control)
- Weekly standings: all teams ranked
- Performance charts: cumulative P&L, win rate trend, calibration curve
- Strategy sharing: when a team outperforms, their signal rationale is visible
- Martin's team visible on leaderboard but marked as "benchmark only"

### 6. Strategy Sharing Protocol
- When any team discovers edge (new city pattern, model weighting, timing optimization), it gets flagged
- Shared via a common "discoveries" feed visible to all teams
- Each team decides independently whether to adopt shared strategies
- The competition + sharing dynamic drives collective improvement

### 7. Cliff & Martin Integration
- Standardized signal format published as a simple spec they can implement
- API endpoint or shared file format for signal submission
- Their signals evaluated against same outcomes as ours
- No access to our Kalshi account — leaderboard comparison only (Martin), rotation eligible (Cliff once stable)

## Prerequisites (must be done FIRST)
- [ ] Paper trade / live trade separation on dashboard (TASK-CLEANUP-10, queued)
- [ ] DB reconciliation with Kalshi reality
- [ ] Standardized P&L tracking across all signal sources
- [ ] Cliff's OpenClaw memory issues resolved

## Deliverable
A markdown design doc at projects/weather-trading/TOURNAMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md that Tim reviews and approves before ANY code is written.

title: Watcher health monitor — auto-restart + alert if weather trading watcher goes down
description:
The model watcher was down for 11+ hours overnight and nobody noticed until Tim checked manually. This is unacceptable for a live trading system.

## What To Build

### 1. Health check script (scripts/watcher_health.sh)
- Check if model_watcher.py process is running
- If dead: restart it automatically with correct env vars (Open-Meteo API key from keychain)
- Log restart events to data/watcher_health.log
- If restart fails 3x in a row: send alert to Henry via openclaw system event

### 2. LaunchAgent (re-enable properly)

- KeepAlive: true (macOS auto-restarts if process dies)
- Set environment variables properly (OPEN_METEO_API_KEY)
- This is the PRIMARY keep-alive mechanism

### 3. Circuit breaker (prevent 429 death spiral)
- If watcher gets 3 consecutive 429 errors: back off for 1 hour, don't keep hammering
- After backoff: resume normal polling
- Log circuit breaker events
- This prevents the scenario that caused us to kill everything yesterday

### 4. Alert on down
- If watcher has been down >15 minutes: send Telegram alert to Tim
- Simple: just check for recent entries in model_watcher.log
- Can be a cron that runs every 15 minutes

## Key Constraint
- The watcher must survive reboots, gateway restarts, and process crashes
- Must NOT cause 429 death spirals (circuit breaker mandatory)
- Must alert humans if it can't self-heal

- Watcher died at 9:20 PM, wasn't restarted until 8:42 AM next day (11+ hours)
- Missed overnight GFS/ECMWF model drops = missed trading opportunities

title: Post-trade audit — Quant reviews every scan cycle for bad bets and risk issues
description:
After every scan cycle places trades, an automated audit runs to catch problems before the next cycle.

## What The Auditor Checks

### 1. Risk/Reward Ratio
- Flag any trade with payout less than 3:1 (risking $2 to make $6 minimum)
- Bracket bets should never appear (now blocked at scanner, but verify)
- Calculate expected value for each trade and flag negative EV

### 2. Position Concentration
- Too many bets in one city? One direction? One date?
- Geographic clustering (is a weather system causing correlated bets?)
- Total exposure vs limits

### 3. Edge Sanity Check
- Is the claimed edge realistic? (>50% edge should be rare and scrutinized)
- Are multiple models actually disagreeing with the market, or is it noise?
- Compare edge at purchase vs historical edge accuracy for similar setups

### 4. Common Sense Checks
- Are we buying contracts that settle TODAY at prices that imply we already lost?
- Are we betting against obvious weather (e.g., "Phoenix below 60°F in summer")
- Do the quantities make sense given Kelly sizing?

## Implementation
- Script: scripts/post_trade_audit.py
- Runs automatically after each scan_and_trade.py or model_watcher scan completes
- Output: PASS (all good) or FLAG (issues found with details)
- On FLAG: alert Henry via system event with specific concerns
- Log all audits to data/trade_audits/ for review

## Integration
- Wire into model_watcher.py: after scan completes, run audit
- Wire into cron_runner.py: after any live trade placement
- Results visible on Trading Desk in Mission Control

## Why This Matters
Tim caught bracket bets with bad risk/reward that the system placed. At $500 it's a lesson. At $5,000+ it's real money lost. The auditor catches these BEFORE scale.
